zh.summary: 看得到資料夾名稱，和能打開裡面的檔案，是兩件事。跟著一個檔案分享案例，學會查資訊、看回應，再說清楚自己確認了什麼。

sourceBody.text: CEH 資安課程 · Module 04 · 初學者完整教學
這一課最重要的觀念：發現某個資源存在，不代表你有權限使用它。
例如，你在公司網路中發現一台檔案伺服器，還查到了名為 Finance（財務部）的共用資料夾。這只能證明你取得了某些資源資訊，不能證明你能開啟資料夾、閱讀薪資資料，或修改任何檔案。
這就是 CEH M04「列舉」最需要建立的判斷能力。
想像你是一名受公司委託的資安工程師，要檢查一棟辦公大樓。
從發現目標到確認權限
這是概念上的學習流程，不是所有工具操作都必須遵守的固定順序。某些服務需要先登入，才能進行列舉。
你要區分五個不同問題：

rows: 服務提供哪些具體資訊？

sourceBody.text: 注意： 公司允許你進行資安測試的「測試授權」，與系統授予測試帳號的「存取權限」是兩回事。即使系統允許連線，也不代表你獲准進行測試。
我們先建立三個基本概念。
IP 位址（IP Address）：用來定位網路上的設備，就像大樓地址。
通訊埠（Port）：用來區分設備上的網路服務入口，就像大樓內不同的服務櫃檯。
SMB（Server Message Block）：一種常見的網路檔案共用協定，Windows 常用它來讓其他電腦存取共用資料夾與印表機等資源。現代 SMB 通常使用 TCP 445。
假設你用 Nmap 掃描練習伺服器：
假設得到：

PORT      STATE   SERVICE
445/tcp   open    microsoft-ds
這代表什麼？
445/tcp 是偵測的通訊埠；open 表示從此次掃描位置觀察到該通訊埠接受連線。
但是 SERVICE 欄位的 microsoft-ds 可能只是 Nmap 根據埠號的服務名稱對照，而不是已經完成 SMB 協定驗證。必須進一步確認服務的實際回應。
[Nmap Network Scanning](https://nmap.org/book/man-version-detection.html)
因此：
TCP 445 開放 ≠ 確認有 SMB 服務 ≠ 確認能存取檔案
假設系統已確認提供 SMB 服務，而且公司提供了合法測試帳號 labuser。
你向服務提出查詢：
「這台伺服器有哪些共用資源？」
伺服器可能回應：

Sharename    Type
---------    ----
Public       Disk
Finance      Disk
這一步就是列舉。
我們沒有要求伺服器交出 Finance 裡的檔案，只是要求列出共用資源的名稱。
Windows 提供的 NetShareEnum 函式正是此類查詢的例子。它可取得伺服器上的 SMB 共用資源資訊，而且分成不同資訊層級：例如 Level 0 回傳名稱、Level 1 可包含類型與說明，較高層級的資訊可能要求額外權限。
[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/lmshare/nf-lmshare-netshareenum)
這裡就可以理解一項重要觀念：
資訊揭露程度與操作權限不是同一個維度。
伺服器可能允許某個帳號知道有 Finance，但不允許它閱讀其中的內容。
我們繼續模擬：
檔案伺服器
已確認服務
Public
測試讀取成功
Finance
測試讀取遭拒
這是模擬結果，代表同一個測試帳號對兩個資源有不同的存取結果。
要解釋原因，先認識兩種 Windows 權限。
第一種：Share Permissions（共用權限）
它控制使用者透過網路共用服務，可以對這個共用資源做哪些操作。
第二種：NTFS Permissions（NTFS 檔案系統權限）
它控制檔案系統中的資料夾與檔案，允許哪些身分讀取、寫入或修改。
經由 SMB 存取 Windows NTFS 檔案時，通常兩種權限都會影響最後結果。不能只看其中一種就下結論。
[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/networking/access-denied-access-smb-file-share)
例如，某帳號具有共用資料夾的讀取權限，但 NTFS 拒絕它讀取某份機密檔案，最終讀取仍可能失敗。
反過來說，即使 NTFS 允許讀取，若共用層級拒絕，透過該 SMB 共用路徑的存取也會被阻擋。
因此，當你看到 Access Denied，你目前只確認了這次操作遭到拒絕。你尚未證明拒絕的確切原因，也不能推論其他使用者一樣無法存取。
以下使用 Windows PowerShell，假設 192.168.56.10 是已經配置好的授權練習主機，且你有適當的測試帳號。
第一步：確認通訊埠
Test-NetConnection 192.168.56.10 -Port 445
如果看到：
TcpTestSucceeded : True
代表這次 TCP 連線測試成功，不代表已經登入檔案伺服器。
[Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/nettcpip/test-netconnection)
第二步：列出共用資源
假設取得：

Share name
----------
Public
Finance
這就完成了一次共用資源列舉。指令會依照目前使用的身分及伺服器設定取得結果，因此不一定每次都能列出資源。
第三步：測試指定檔案的讀取權限
Get-Content '\\192.168.56.10\Public\demo.txt'
如果成功顯示檔案內容，就能確認目前使用的身分，在這次測試條件下，可以讀取該檔案。
再測試預先約定的另一個檔案：
Get-Content '\\192.168.56.10\Finance\demo.txt'
如果回覆 Access is denied，記錄這次遭拒即可，不要因此就擅自更換帳號或嘗試繞過權限。
如果你使用 Ubuntu/Linux，也可以利用 Samba 的 smbclient 指令進行共用名稱列舉：
smbclient -L 192.168.56.10 -U labuser
指令會要求輸入該測試帳號的密碼。-L 代表列出伺服器提供的資源，它本身不是讀取檔案內容的操作。
[Samba](https://www.samba.org/samba/docs/current/man-html/smbclient.1.html)
列舉的結果需要放進安全性脈絡中解讀。
假設一個普通員工帳號可以列出整家公司所有部門共用資料夾的名稱，這可能暴露一些組織資訊，但不一定構成嚴重漏洞。
真正應該調查的是：這些名稱是否敏感、業務是否需要揭露、其他未授權使用者是否也能取得，以及系統是否有不必要的檔案存取權限。
從防護角度，可採用三個層次：

items: 網路限制：僅允許需要使用 SMB 的設備與使用者網段連線。
最小權限：對帳號、共用資料夾與實際檔案分別設定必要的權限。
安全稽核：在適當配置的 Windows 系統中，可利用事件 ID 5140 觀察共用存取，利用 5145 觀察共用層級的詳細存取檢查；但 NTFS 層級的拒絕還需要對應的檔案系統稽核，不能只依賴 5145。

sourceBody.text: [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-5145)
最後，資安報告至少要記錄測試時間、來源與目標、使用帳號、查詢指令、實際結果，以及測試限制。
要避免直接寫「Finance 已被攻破」這種沒有證據支持的結論。
現在學的是列舉的共同原理。接下來你會在不同服務看到同樣的概念：

rows: 共用資料夾、部分伺服器資訊
目錄服務中的帳號、群組、物件
設備資訊、介面與管理資料
郵件服務允許查詢的資訊

sourceBody.text: 它們使用不同協定，但問題本質相同：服務會向什麼身分透露哪些資訊？這些資訊是否超過業務需要？

en.summary: Seeing a folder’s name and opening a file inside it are different things. Follow a file-sharing example to learn what to ask, what to look for, and how to describe what you found.

sections.heading: 1. You found Public and Finance. What can you do next?
paragraphs: Start with a made-up practice scenario. You sign in to a file server with a test account named labuser and see two share names: Public and Finance. A server is a computer that provides a service. A share is a file-sharing location you can connect to over the network.

Using SMB—the rules for this kind of network file sharing—you try to download the agreed test.txt file from each share. Public succeeds. Finance returns ACCESS_DENIED: that read request was rejected. The record below keeps those observations separate.

blocks.heading: Start with the result: one account, two file reads
paragraphs: Assume the test is authorized and labuser has signed in successfully. This is a simplified teaching record. In your own lab, save the tool’s actual output.
You can report: “labuser could see the Finance share name, and its attempt to read Finance/test.txt was denied.” Directory listings, other files, and writing each need their own results.

Querying a service for details such as share names, accounts, or groups is called enumeration. Think of getting a department list at reception: entering an office, reading files, and editing them each require permission. Security teams use enumeration to inventory resources and check who can see them.
blocks.code:
445/tcp open
SMB protocol response confirmed
Share names: Public, Finance
\\fileserver\Public\test.txt  → Read successful
\\fileserver\Finance\test.txt → ACCESS_DENIED

sections.heading: 2. Break the result into five steps
paragraphs: Scanning is like checking which reception desk responds. Enumeration is asking that desk for a list. Reconnaissance comes earlier: gathering background such as company names, domains, or system purposes. A tool may do several of these jobs at once; keep their results separate.

Before testing, agree on the host, time, account, and allowed operations. Sign in when the service requires it. Some services allow anonymous queries; record that identity too. The five steps below organize your reasoning, rather than prescribe how every tool works.

blocks.caption: From an open endpoint to a specific file read
blocks.description: Start with permission to test. Record the identity and response at every step, and sign in whenever required.

items.title: Find an endpoint
items.body: TCP 445 is open: the probe observed a program accepting connections.

items.title: Check the protocol
items.body: A response using SMB gives you evidence that the service speaks SMB.

items.title: List share names
items.body: Public and Finance appear: record the names visible to this identity.

items.title: List a directory
items.body: Run ls and record the entries returned for that directory.

items.title: Read a test file
items.body: Run get and record whether the specified file downloads successfully.

blocks.caption: Four foundational terms
rows: An endpoint number, used together with an IP address and transport protocol
A program or capability that does a job
Rules both sides use to exchange messages
A specific item the service manages

blocks.heading: The port is a clue; check the response
paragraphs: TCP is one protocol used to carry data. A result of 445/tcp open tells you that a program accepted connections during this probe. SMB commonly uses TCP 445; inspect the protocol response next.

Nmap probes hosts and services. Its -sV option tries to identify a service and version. Keep the original response alongside the tool’s identification so you can review what supports it. [Port states](https://nmap.org/book/man-port-scanning-basics.html) · [Service detection](https://nmap.org/book/man-version-detection.html)

blocks.heading: Further detail: NetShareEnum information levels
paragraphs: An API is an interface a program uses to request a function from another program. Microsoft’s NetShareEnum is one way to query shares. Its information level selects which fields to request.
Level 0 returns share names. Level 1 adds resource type and a comment. Higher levels request other information, with permissions depending on calling context and platform.

“No special group membership required” for levels 0/1 concerns group membership. Whether an anonymous query succeeds still depends on authentication and service policy. [NetShareEnum documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/lmshare/nf-lmshare-netshareenum)

sections.heading: 3. Separate “Who are you?” from “What may you do?”
paragraphs: Authentication checks who you are, for example when labuser signs in with a password. Authorization decides what that account may do, such as read or edit a file. Permission to conduct a test is the agreement made beforehand; sign-in and access rights are checks the system performs. [Authentication and authorization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/authentication-vs-authorization)
Each card below asks a different question about Finance. They summarize the made-up case and keep the untested actions visible.

Typical Windows SMB access depends on both share permissions and NTFS permissions. Share permissions govern access through the network share. NTFS is a Windows file system; its permissions govern folders and files. If the share allows reading and writing but NTFS allows only reading, access through that path is normally read-only. Also check group membership, rules inherited from parent folders, and allow/deny settings.

When you receive ACCESS_DENIED, record the specific action that was denied. Then check whether sign-in succeeded, review SMB policy and share/NTFS permissions, and use logs to locate the cause. [Troubleshooting steps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/networking/access-denied-access-smb-file-share)

blocks.caption: Finance: four actions, four separate results
blocks.description: A made-up case using labuser. Each card describes one action. Record a new result when the account, path, or conditions change.

items.title: See the name
items.body: labuser · Finance: Observed: Finance appeared in the share list.

items.title: List the directory
items.body: labuser · Finance: To check: record the ls response inside Finance.

items.title: Read a file
items.body: labuser · Finance/test.txt: Observed: reading Finance/test.txt was denied.

items.title: Write a file
items.body: labuser · Finance: To check: obtain permission for this action and test it separately.

blocks.heading: Where should you look when a read fails?
paragraphs: Assuming labuser has signed in successfully, check whether the share permits the read, then whether NTFS permits reading that file. Include any other applicable policies when interpreting the result. This is a troubleshooting guide; the system’s internal check order depends on its implementation.

blocks.heading: Further detail: ABE filters items inside a share
paragraphs: Access-Based Enumeration (ABE) filters the visibility of files and folders inside a share according to access rights. SMB FolderEnumerationMode=AccessBased controls this behavior.

This setting filters items inside Finance. Listing the server’s share names is a separate query. Access controls still decide whether a file operation is allowed. [FolderEnumerationMode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/smbshare/set-smbshare?view=windowsserver2025-ps)

sections.heading: 4. Try it: record a result after each command
paragraphs: Use an Ubuntu/Linux computer with Nmap and smbclient installed. smbclient connects to SMB services. Prepare an authorized server, the labuser test account, and a synthetic Public/test.txt file on the server.

Agree on the host, time, allowed actions, stop conditions, and records you may keep. The address 192.0.2.10 is reserved for examples. Replace it in every command with your authorized lab host. [Documentation addresses](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5737)

Enter the commands in a terminal and enter your password only when prompted. Remove passwords and personal information from saved records. The earlier case was illustrative; record what you actually observe here.

blocks.heading: A. Observe port and service
paragraphs: -p 445 selects TCP 445, and -sV tries to identify the service and version. Find those results in the output and save the original response. An open result establishes a responding endpoint; check the protocol evidence next.

blocks.heading: B. List share names
paragraphs: -L asks for a share list, and -U selects the account. Enter the password at the prompt, then find the share names in the response. If Public and Finance appear, record that labuser’s query returned those two names.

blocks.heading: C. Prepare a download directory in your local terminal
paragraphs: Run this small block in your local terminal. mktemp -d creates a fresh temporary directory. lab_dir stores its path, cd enters it, and pwd prints your current location.

If creation or navigation fails, the block prints STOP. Resolve the error before moving on. On success, it prints the new directory’s path. Check that downloaded-test.txt does not already exist there before downloading.
blocks.code:
if lab_dir=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$lab_dir"; then
  pwd
else
  printf "%s\n" "STOP: prepare the local directory first."
fi

blocks.heading: D. Connect to Public on the same server
paragraphs: After the previous step succeeds, enter this command in the same local terminal and type the password when prompted. A successful connection gives you the smb: prompt. Use the next step’s commands there.

blocks.heading: E. List and read at the smb: prompt
paragraphs: At the smb: prompt, enter one command at a time. ls lists entries in the current server directory. get reads the prepared, authorized test.txt and saves it as downloaded-test.txt in your current local directory. quit closes the connection.

Check each response before continuing. A successful ls establishes a directory listing. A successful get establishes the download of that specific synthetic file. If access is denied, save the message and path, then use the previous section to investigate.

blocks.heading: Record and finish
paragraphs: Save the time, host, account, path, command, and response together. If Finance is also in scope, test its synthetic file in the same way. Confirm permission separately before testing creation, writing, or deletion.
After disconnecting, keep the agreed report and remove your downloaded synthetic file and temporary directory. These steps read server data; cleanup applies to the local copy.

blocks.heading: Tool option: why use interactive mode?
paragraphs: The Samba manual states that -c implies -N (no password prompt). This lesson uses an interactive connection followed by ls, get and quit so that the prompt and each response are clear. [Official smbclient manual](https://www.samba.org/samba/docs/current/man-html/smbclient.1.html)

blocks.caption: Review your notes: what does each result establish?
rows: This probe observed a port accepting connections
The querying identity can see the share name
Denial layer, other files and other operations

sections.heading: 5. Decide whether the information exposure is a risk
paragraphs: Start with the intended audience. Employees may be expected to see department shares. If an outside visitor can also retrieve sensitive department or employee information, investigate who can reach it and why.

Consider five things together: how sensitive the information is, who can query it, who policy allows to see it, which networks can reach it, and how it could be used. Write down the observation first, then explain the evidence behind your risk judgment.

MITRE ATT&CK is a knowledge base of common adversary behavior. Network share discovery maps to [T1135](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1135/); account discovery maps to [T1087](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087/). Legitimate inventory work may use similar queries, so include authorization and context in your assessment.

Use three layers of protection: limit network access, return only the information people need, and set appropriate rights for actions such as reading and editing. Use logs—records of system events—to investigate unusual bursts of queries. After a change, retest with authorized accounts to check that restrictions work and legitimate work still succeeds.

blocks.heading: Further detail: audit scope of 5140 and 5145
paragraphs: Auditing tells the server which events to record. Enable the relevant audit policies before relying on event IDs. Event 5140 provides context for the first share-access attempt in a session, such as the account, source address, and share. To trace individual file reads, also check the evidence recorded at the file-access layer.

Event 5145 (Audit Detailed File Share) records share-object access checks; its failure events concern denial at the share layer. An NTFS denial does not automatically generate a 5145 failure event; examine filesystem auditing and related responses separately.

Preserve time, target, identity, operation and response together. Record a new result when changing identity or network location. [5140 documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-5140) · [5145 documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-10/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-5145)

sections.heading: 6. Use the same questions in the next lesson
paragraphs: For any service, ask: “Which service am I querying? What specific information did it return? What can this account do under these conditions?” Use the table as a reference; later lessons introduce each service in turn.

Use the [EC-Council CEH course](https://www.eccouncil.org/train-certify/certified-ethical-hacker-ceh/) and [Exam Blueprint v5.0](https://cert.eccouncil.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/CEH-Exam-Blueprint-v5.pdf) to check enumeration scope. This site’s twelve M04 core topics are an editorial teaching sequence; concept counts vary by module.

The next core topic remains M04-02 DNS enumeration. Accounts, groups, permissions and Active Directory are related further reading, connecting later to LDAP, privilege escalation and lateral movement.

blocks.caption: Common query targets
rows: Mail-service information; recipient verification under specific configurations
Interfaces, endpoints and available remote procedure services

sections.heading: 7. Test: three understanding checks
paragraphs: Choose an answer and think of a reason before opening the explanation. Opening it only shows the teaching answer. Your response and understanding can be discussed separately afterward.

The original small check remains useful as a verbal explanation: after listing Finance but being denied a specific file read, how would you explain the confirmed result and the permissions that still need checking?

en.prompt: smbclient listed Finance successfully, but no file has been opened. What is the most accurate conclusion?
options: Read access to Finance has been obtained
The Finance share name was visible in this query
A high-risk vulnerability in Finance has been confirmed
Administrator access to Finance has been obtained
rationales: A: Reading a specific file is a separate operation requiring an observed result.
B: Correct. The response tells us this account could see the share name.
C: To judge the risk, check the policy, the sensitivity of the information, and how it could be used.
D: Administrative access requires separate evidence.

en.prompt: labuser receives ACCESS_DENIED when reading Finance/test.txt. Which inference is least reasonable?
options: This particular file read did not succeed
Effective permissions and the cause of denial should be checked
labuser certainly cannot perform any operation on Finance
Other users may receive different results
rationales: A: This is what the response tells you.
B: Identity, policy, share/NTFS permissions and logs help locate the denial.
C: Correct choice. A denied read tells you about that read. Other actions need their own checks.
D: Different identities may have different permissions; observe them separately.

en.prompt: Two accounts query the same share on the same server and receive different results. What should be investigated first?
rationales: A: CPU speed is not the priority permission variable in this case.
B: Correct. Compare accounts, groups, authorization policy and other query conditions.
C: Screen resolution has no direct role in server-side authorization.
D: Disk speed normally concerns performance; identity and policy are the first focus here.
